summary: Victor B. Lieberman is a historian who earned a BA from Yale University (~1963–1967) and a PhD from SOAS University of London (~1971–1976). In 1984, he became a Distinguished University Professor of History at the University of Michigan.

Victor Chan is a Tibetologist who studied as a graduate student at the University of Chicago. He founded the Dalai Lama Center for Peace and Education in 2005 and served as Executive Director of UBC's Contemporary Tibetan Studies Program (attested 2005).
Victor Cousin was a philosopher who studied at Lycée Charlemagne until 1810 and Pensionnat normal (~1810–1812). He served on the faculty at the University of Paris from circa 1815 to 1851.

Victor Forte is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed his Ph.D. at Temple University in 2004. In 2007, he was attested as an Assistant Professor in the Department of Religious Studies at Albright College.

Victor Goloubew was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Saint Petersburg University (~1895–1899) and Heidelberg University (Ph.D. 1901–1904). He taught at INALCO (~1913–1914), the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1920–1943).

Victor H. Mair studied at Dartmouth, SOAS, and Harvard (Ph.D. ~1973–1976) under Patrick Hanan and James Robert Hightower. He worked in sinology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies, teaching at Harvard (~1976–1979) and the University of Pennsylvania from 1979.

Victor Hehn was a scholar of linguistics and history who studied at the University of Tartu (~1830–1834). He later held posts at the University of Tartu (~1846–1851) and the National Library of Russia (1855–1873).

Victor Henry was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Strasbourg, Burgundy, and Paris, where he was mentored by Abel Bergaigne. He held appointments at the University of Douai, University of Lille, and the University of Paris from 1888.

Victor Herbert Jackson was an Indologist and historian who joined the Indian Education Service in 1900. He taught at Presidency University (~1900–1907) and served as Principal of Patna College from circa 1907 to 1927.

Linguist Victor Michels studied in Berlin under Paul Deussen, Heidelberg under Hermann Osthoff, and Leipzig (PhD 1886–1889) under Brugmann, Leskien, and Windisch. He served as PD at Göttingen (1892) and Professor of German Philology at Jena (1895).

Victor Turner was an anthropologist of religion who earned degrees at UCL and the University of Manchester. He held academic posts at the University of Manchester (~1955–1963), Cornell (1963), the University of Chicago (1968–1977), and the University of Virginia (1977).

Victoria Vertogradova is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Mikhail Nikolayevich Peterson. She is attested in 2026 as a Chief Scientific Officer at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya was an Indian scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He held posts as a Pandit and supervisor of collation at Visva-Bharati University (attested 1929–1944) and as Asutosh Professor of Sanskrit at Calcutta University (attested 1941–1943).

Vidya Dehejia is an art historian and Indologist who studied at Cambridge (PhD ~1963–1968). She held posts at Hong Kong, the Smithsonian Institution, and Columbia University, where she became Barbara Stoler Miller Professor of Indian Art in 2002.

Vidya Niwas Mishra was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Allahabad, Gorakhpur, and under Paul Thieme and Kshetresh Chandra Chattopadhyaya. He served as Professor of Linguistics at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and Vice-Chancellor of Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith.

Vijay Singh is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned a Doctor of Philosophy at Panjab University (1998–2002). He was appointed Professor and Chairperson at Panjab University in 1994.
Vijaya Indra Suri was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who succeeded Vijaya Dharma Suri (attested 1933) and founded the Prakrit Text Society.
Vijayalakshmi Mani is a researcher in Indology and history who is attested in 2026 as a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, studying under doctoral supervisor V. Yamuna Devi.
Viktor Iosifovich Balin was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University from circa 1946 to 1951, where he began teaching in 1952.

Vilgelm Mikhailovich Berner was an Indologist who studied at the Leningrad Oriental Institute in 1931. From 1935 to 1936, he was an aspirant at the Institute of Anthropology at Moscow State University.
